day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight AC lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Head directly from Trudeau Airport to your accommodation in Old Montreal via the 747 express bus (budget-friendly ~$10 CAD). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a self-guided walk around the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: Dive straight into the neighborhood with the Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk. Wander Place Jacques-Cartier, admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free), and sample poutine, smoked meat bites, and maple taffy from street vendors along Rue Saint-Paul. This iconic walk is perfect for first-timers and very wallet-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Events: July 15 falls right in the heart of the Just for Laughs Festival! Head to the free outdoor stages near Saint-Denis and Sainte-Catherine streets (a short Metro ride from Old Montreal) for world-class comedy performances, street acts, and a buzzing festival atmosphere — all completely free.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick coffee and croissant at a café near the airport before boarding.
meals.lunch: Pick up a classic poutine from La Banquise takeout window or a street vendor in Old Montreal (~$12–15 CAD) during your afternoon walk.
meals.dinner: Grab a smoked meat sandwich and pickle at a casual deli near the Just for Laughs festival zone, or try a food truck on Sainte-Catherine Street (~$10–15 CAD). Look for festival food stalls for local flavors at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.notes: The 747 express bus from the airport runs 24/7 and connects to the Metro system — buy a 3-day transit pass (~$21 CAD) on Day 2 to save money on transport. Just for Laughs outdoor stages are FREE — no tickets needed. Keep an eye on the festival schedule at hahaha.com for the best free shows on this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the Metro Orange Line north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Spend the morning exploring stalls overflowing with Quebec cheeses, fresh fruit, maple products, artisan bread, and local charcuterie. Sample generously — vendors are happy to offer tastes. Budget ~$15–20 CAD for samples and small purchases to take back to the room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End & Plateau Neighborhood Exploration: From Jean-Talon, walk or bike (BIXI bike share ~$7/day) through the trendy Mile End and Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhoods. Browse colorful murals, visit Saint-Viateur Bagel (an iconic Montreal institution) for a fresh wood-fired bagel, and explore Parc Laurier for a relaxing afternoon picnic in the warm summer weather (25°C — perfect outdoor conditions).
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Events (Round 2): Return to the Just for Laughs Festival for another evening of free outdoor performances. Tonight, explore the Village des Arts section for interactive installations and impromptu street comedy. The festival runs late into the night, so enjoy the lively atmosphere along with locals.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh bagel with cream cheese and lox at Saint-Viateur Bagel on your way to or from Jean-Talon (~$5–7 CAD). A Montreal institution and incredibly budget-friendly.
meals.lunch: Assemble a picnic from Jean-Talon Market stalls: local cheese, fresh bread, fruit, and a can of local cider (~$12–15 CAD total). Eat in the market's outdoor seating area or carry it to Parc Laurier.
meals.dinner: Try Au Pied de Cochon's more affordable neighbor — head to a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant in Plateau, where corkage is free and meals are ~$15–20 CAD. Look for 'Apportez Votre Vin' signs for the best budget dining deals in Montreal.

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bike share is Montreal's public bike system — a 24-hour pass costs ~$7 CAD and is great for covering the Plateau and Mile End. Jean-Talon Market is open daily but most vibrant on weekday mornings. Bring a small reusable bag for market purchases. Weather forecast is warm (25°C) with minimal rain — ideal for outdoor markets and cycling.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park Hike: Start the day with an energizing hike up Mont Royal — the green heart of Montreal. The summit offers a breathtaking panoramic view of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River. The park is completely free to enter. Take the Camillien-Houde trail (~45 min to the top) and enjoy the warm morning air before the midday heat sets in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Atwater Market & Lachine Canal Walk: Descend from Mont Royal and head to Atwater Market near the Lachine Canal. Browse local vendors selling Quebec produce, artisan goods, and specialty foods. Then take a leisurely walk or rent a BIXI bike along the flat, scenic Lachine Canal path — a former industrial waterway now lined with cafés and parks. The canal path is free and one of Montreal's best-kept budget gems.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival — Gala Night Atmosphere & Free Shows: Friday night at Just for Laughs is electric. While ticketed galas happen indoors, the outdoor festival zone explodes with free performances, roving comedians, and live music. Join the crowd on Rue Saint-Denis for the best street energy of the festival week. Grab a cold local beer from a festival vendor and enjoy the show.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local dépanneur (corner store) or boulangerie near Old Montreal for a coffee and pain au chocolat (~$4–6 CAD) before heading to Mont Royal.
meals.lunch: Eat at Atwater Market — pick up a Québécois sausage, fresh baguette, and local mustard for a canal-side picnic (~$10–13 CAD). Alternatively, the market's prepared food counters offer affordable hot meals.
meals.dinner: Head to Chinatown (a short Metro ride from Old Montreal) for a filling and ultra-budget dinner. Pho, dim sum, or Vietnamese banh mi sandwiches run ~$10–14 CAD and portions are generous. Try Kim Fung or a similar local spot on Rue de la Gauchetière.

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal Park is free and open year-round. The hike is moderate — wear comfortable walking shoes. Lachine Canal bike path is flat and family-friendly; BIXI stations are available at both Atwater Market and along the canal. Friday night at Just for Laughs is typically the busiest and most exciting — arrive by 8:00 PM to secure a good spot near the outdoor stages.

day_by_day.morning: Old Port & Bonsecours Market Exploration: Spend your final morning exploring the Old Port waterfront — a beautiful stretch along the St. Lawrence River with historic architecture, street performers, and public art. Visit the exterior of Marché Bonsecours (free), Montreal's iconic silver-domed public market, now home to Quebec artisans. Browse for affordable locally made souvenirs like maple candy, artisan jams, or small crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Just for Laughs Festival — Final Afternoon Free Events: Catch the final afternoon programming of the Just for Laughs Festival before it winds down for the weekend. The outdoor stages typically feature some of the best free acts on Saturday afternoons. Explore any remaining festival installations, grab a final festival snack, and soak in the celebratory summer atmosphere with locals and visitors alike.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal & Evening Stroll: End your Montreal trip with a leisurely dinner in Old Montreal. As the sun sets, the cobblestone streets and gas-lit lanterns create a magical atmosphere. Take a final evening walk along the waterfront, watch the lights reflect on the St. Lawrence River, and enjoy a last maple-flavored treat from a street vendor as a sweet send-off.

meals.breakfast: Try Olive et Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved local bakery with excellent sandwiches and pastries. Arrive early as it gets busy. Budget ~$10–12 CAD for a coffee and pastry or light sandwich.
meals.lunch: Grab a classic Montreal smoked meat sandwich from a casual spot near the festival zone or a food truck in the Old Port (~$12–15 CAD). Schwartz's Deli is the legendary choice (expect a line) or opt for a nearby deli for a shorter wait.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for your farewell meal at a BYOB restaurant in Old Montreal. Look for fixed-price table d'hôte menus (often $20–28 CAD for 2–3 courses) — excellent value and a true Québécois dining experience. Pick up a bottle of local wine from a nearby SAQ (Société des alcools du Québec) to bring along.

day_by_day.notes: Check festival closing times and any special Saturday events at hahaha.com before heading out. The Old Port is busiest on Saturday afternoons — arrive at Bonsecours Market early to avoid crowds. If departing on a later flight, the 747 bus back to the airport runs frequently. Consider leaving your bags at the hotel's luggage storage to enjoy your final hours unencumbered. Total estimated daily budget: ~$50–70 CAD per day including transit, food, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight AC lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Head from the airport to your Old Montreal hotel via the 747 express bus or a rideshare (~30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the charming Vieux-Montréal neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, dive straight into the neighborhood on foot. Join or self-guide a walk along the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal, sampling iconic Quebec street food — poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and maple-glazed treats — while soaking in the 17th-century architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier and the Old Port waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Events: July 15 falls right in the heart of the Just for Laughs Festival (held annually mid-July). Head to the free outdoor stages near Saint-Denis and Sainte-Catherine streets for world-class street performers, comedians, and a buzzing festival atmosphere. A perfect low-cost, high-energy introduction to Montreal's summer scene.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or on arrival — a café au lait and croissant from a terminal café.
meals.lunch: During the Old Montreal walk, pick up a classic poutine from La Banquise's Old Port outpost or grab a smoked meat sandwich from a nearby deli counter (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dine at Olive & Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved local bistro known for creative sandwiches, fresh salads, and Quebec-inspired plates. Mid-range pricing (~$25–35 CAD per person). Reserve ahead if possible.

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 13:00, keep the afternoon relaxed and walkable — everything is within steps of your Old Montreal hotel. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for cobblestones. Check the Just for Laughs schedule online before heading out to catch the best free outdoor acts.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro from Old Montreal (Orange Line north) to Jean-Talon station. Spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, artisan charcuterie, local fruits, and freshly baked goods. Engage with vendors, learn about Quebec's food culture, and pick up snacks for later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Bagel & Brunch Crawl: From Jean-Talon, walk or take a short bus ride into the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Visit the legendary St-Viateur Bagel and Fairmount Bagel bakeries — two iconic rivals — to taste Montreal's wood-fired, hand-rolled bagels. Explore the indie boutiques, street art, and café culture of this eclectic district before heading back toward downtown.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Events (continued): Return to the festival hub for another evening of free outdoor comedy and street performances. If budget allows, consider upgrading to a ticketed indoor show featuring a headlining comedian (~$40–70 CAD) for a fuller festival experience.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Jean-Talon Market itself — grab a fresh pastry, local cheese, and fruit from market vendors for a delicious and affordable morning spread (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.lunch: In Mile End, stop at Beauty's Luncheonette, a Montreal institution since 1942, for a classic brunch plate — eggs, smoked salmon, and a fresh bagel (~$20–28 CAD).
meals.dinner: Try Damas Restaurant in Mile End for elevated Syrian-Mediterranean cuisine — a local favourite with generous portions and mid-range pricing (~$35–45 CAD per person). Alternatively, grab casual Lebanese street food from a nearby Mile End spot for a lighter budget option.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest and most vibrant in the morning — arrive by 9:30–10:00 AM for the best experience. The market-to-Mile End route is very walkable and bikeable; consider renting a BIXI bike (Montreal's public bike share) for a fun and affordable way to travel between neighborhoods.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park & Belvedere Lookout: Start the day with a refreshing morning hike or walk up Mont Royal, Montreal's iconic green hill. Follow the Olmsted Trail to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River. The warm summer weather (25°C) makes this a perfect outdoor morning activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal & Rue Saint-Denis Exploration: Descend from the mountain and wander through the vibrant Plateau neighborhood. Browse the boutiques, bookstores, and galleries along Rue Saint-Denis and Avenue du Mont-Royal. Pop into local shops for Quebec-made souvenirs — maple products, local art prints, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival — Outdoor Spectacle Night: Friday evenings at Just for Laughs typically feature larger free outdoor spectacles and themed street parties. Head back to the festival zone for the biggest crowd energy of the week. Enjoy live music, roaming performers, and the electric summer festival atmosphere Montreal is famous for.

meals.breakfast: Before heading to the mountain, stop at Café Olimpico in Mile End (a local espresso institution) or Crew Collective & Café downtown for a strong coffee and a fresh pastry (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.lunch: In the Plateau, grab a meal at L'Express — a classic French-style Montreal bistro on Rue Saint-Denis, beloved by locals for its steak tartare, duck confit, and affordable prix-fixe lunch (~$25–35 CAD).
meals.dinner: Enjoy dinner at Schwartz's Deli on Boulevard Saint-Laurent — the legendary smoked meat institution. Expect a short queue, communal seating, and an unforgettable smoked meat sandwich with coleslaw and a pickle (~$20–25 CAD). A true Montreal bucket-list meal.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen and bring water for the Mont Royal hike — the summit can be exposed and warm in July. The mountain has free entry and is a beloved local gathering spot, especially on weekends. BIXI bikes are available near the mountain's base for easy onward travel to the Plateau.

day_by_day.morning: Old Port & Notre-Dame Basilica: Spend your final morning revisiting the beauty of Old Montreal at a leisurely pace. Visit the stunning Basilique Notre-Dame de Montréal (entry ~$10 CAD) for its breathtaking neo-Gothic interior. Afterward, stroll along the Old Port waterfront promenade, watch the St. Lawrence River, and browse the weekend artisan market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Atwater Market & Lachine Canal Walk: Take a short rideshare or metro ride to Atwater Market — a beloved local food hall and outdoor market near the Lachine Canal. Pick up Quebec artisan products, local honey, and fresh produce. Walk or rent a BIXI bike along the scenic Lachine Canal bike path, a converted industrial waterway lined with parks and historic locks.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: Return to your home base for a memorable final dinner. Explore the restaurant-lined streets of Vieux-Montréal for a relaxed, celebratory meal before wrapping up your trip.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full brunch at Arthurs Nosh Bar in the Plateau or grab fresh pastries and a café au lait from Olive & Gourmando (a local favourite) in Old Montreal (~$15–22 CAD).
meals.lunch: At Atwater Market, assemble a picnic from the market vendors — local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and fruit — and enjoy it along the Lachine Canal. A quintessentially Montreal experience (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: End your trip with dinner at Garde Manger in Old Montreal — a lively, mid-upscale seafood-focused restaurant by celebrity chef Chuck Hughes, known for its festive atmosphere and Quebec-sourced ingredients (~$40–55 CAD per person). Book ahead for Saturday evening.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets at both Atwater and Old Port are at their liveliest — a great opportunity for last-minute local souvenirs and food finds. If your return flight is the next day, confirm checkout time with your hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed for a stress-free final evening. The warm July weather makes outdoor dining on a terrace a wonderful option.

meals.lunch: Cuisine brassée at Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — Chef Chuck Hughes' celebrated bistro featuring locally sourced seafood and Quebec charcuterie. Perfect first taste of Montreal's premium food scene.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's landmark fine-dining institution by Chef Normand Laprise. Seasonal tasting menu showcasing the finest Quebec ingredients. Reserve well in advance. Located steps from Old Montreal.

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 13:00; allow 60–75 minutes for baggage, customs, and private transfer to Old Montreal. Pre-book private airport transfer for a seamless luxury arrival. Toqué! reservations are essential — book months ahead for July.

Join a premium guided food tour sampling Quebec artisan cheeses, fresh maple products, heirloom fruits, local charcuterie, and freshly baked goods. Meet passionate local producers and learn about Quebec's rich agricultural heritage. The market is a sensory feast in peak summer season.

Visit iconic wood-fired bagel bakeries — St-Viateur and Fairmount — and explore the eclectic cafés, boutiques, and street art of this creative district. Stroll along Avenue du Parc and soak in the neighborhood's unique Franco-Jewish cultural heritage.

Dress smartly and enjoy pre-show cocktails at the venue bar.

meals.breakfast: Crew Collective & Café or Olive + Gourmando (Old Montreal) — artisan pastries, specialty coffee, and fresh-pressed juices in a stunning heritage bank building or beloved local café.
meals.lunch: Maison Publique (Mile End) — Derek Dammann's celebrated gastropub known for its exceptional seasonal menu, house-made charcuterie, and curated natural wine list. A Mile End institution.
meals.dinner: Le Filet (Plateau-Mont-Royal) — intimate, upscale seafood-focused restaurant with a refined small-plates menu and outstanding wine pairings. Ideal pre-show or post-show dining.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best visited early morning when vendors are freshest. Book a private or small-group premium food tour in advance. Just for Laughs ticketed shows sell out quickly in July — purchase tickets before the trip.

Visit the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica (book the AURA immersive light show experience for the evening if desired). Browse the upscale galleries and boutiques along Rue Saint-Paul. Stop at the Old Port waterfront for a morning stroll along the promenade with views of the St. Lawrence River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury food and wine experience: Book a curated private tasting session at a renowned Old Montreal restaurant or wine bar — such as a sommelier-led Quebec wine and cheese pairing at Philémon Bar or a private chef's table experience. day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Gala: Attend one of the prestigious televised Gala events — the pinnacle of the festival experience — featuring top-tier international comedians in an elegant theater setting. meals.breakfast: In-room or hotel breakfast — indulge in a leisurely room-service spread or visit the hotel's restaurant for eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed juices, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Chez l'Épicier (Old Montreal) — a beloved Old Montreal gem blending market-fresh cuisine with creative Quebec flavors in a chic, intimate setting. Excellent prix-fixe lunch menu.
meals.dinner: Pastel (Old Montreal or downtown) — one of Montreal's hottest new fine-dining destinations, offering inventive tasting menus with bold flavors and impeccable plating. Book the chef's counter for the full experience.

A perfect way to unwind on your last full afternoon in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening celebration dinner followed by a sunset stroll through Old Montreal. End the night with cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the city skyline and river.
